commands:
starbridge ask \
  --question 'How long should deleted notes stay in the trash before auto-purge?' \
  --context 'Trash never purges today and the storage bill doubled. Each month of trash retention costs about $20/month at today’s volume; 85% of support restore requests come within 3 weeks of the delete.
7 days: cheapest (~$5/month) but blocks most restores.
30 days: covers the 3-week window for 85% of restores with margin, ~$20/month.
90 days: safest for restores, ~$60/month.' \
  --option '7 days' --option '30 days' --option '90 days' --waiting
turns.final: Done and verified. The owner chose 7 days via the card, so I set the retention to 7 days in src/trash.js:3. Every `remove()` now sweeps out notes older than that (src/trash.js:7), so the trash purges itself with no scheduler needed, and `purge()` is exported if you later want to run it on a cron. Quick check confirmed an 8-day-old note is purged, a 6-day-old one kept. At current volume this caps trash at ~$5/month instead of growing forever.
